#HPMV: A thread! 
Q. What is HPMV?
A. Human Metapneumovirus is a RNA virus which causes a disease similar to that of the corona virus, i.e. cough, fever, running nose, sore throat and which is often self limiting. 1/6

nodes.author: drtandon07
nodes.text:
Q. How does HPMV spread?
A. It spreads via both droplet infection (coughing, sneezing, talking) and through fomites (transmission through non living objects like door knobs, chairs, etc on which the virus might survive)
(2/6)

nodes.author: drtandon07
nodes.text:
Q. Do we have any vaccine against HPMV? Is there an effective/specific treatment available?

A. The answer to both the questions is NO. But as already stated, the disease is self limiting, i.e. resolves on its own.
(3/6)

nodes.author: drtandon07
nodes.text:
Q. Who are the most vulnerable group? 

A. Young children below 5 years of age, elderly above 60 years of age and immunocompromised individuals (individuals who have a chronic disease)
(4/6)

nodes.author: drtandon07
nodes.text:
Q. How can we prevent ourselves from HPMV? 

A. Use a N-95 mask at crowded places and wash hands frequently.
(5/6)

nodes.author: drtandon07
nodes.text:
Q. The most important question: Is there any cause to worry as of now? 

A. No! HPMV has been in circulation in India since 2001 and has been causing seasonal flu since then. There are no confirmed reports that the virus has mutated and/or has caused widespread mortality!
(6/6)
